from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
import numpy as np

# Prepare the data for regression
# Extract the latest year's data (2015) for simplicity
education_expenditure_2015 = education_expenditure['2015 [YR2015]']
gni_per_capita_2015 = gni_per_capita['2015 [YR2015]']
economic_output_2015 = economic_output['2015 [YR2015]']

# Combine the variables into a single DataFrame
data = pd.DataFrame({
    'Education_Expenditure': education_expenditure_2015,
    'GNI_per_Capita': gni_per_capita_2015,
    'Economic_Output': economic_output_2015
})

# Drop rows with missing values
data = data.dropna()

# Prepare the data for regression
X = data[['Education_Expenditure', 'GNI_per_Capita']]
y = data['Economic_Output']

# Create a linear regression model
model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(X, y)

# Get the coefficients
coefficients = model.coef_
